why: The lookahead's own rung on the 30-health content (ADR 0068). The standings moved with the health: on the benchmark seeds, content 4ab506fa, the lookahead with the built-in weights scores 0.516 against greedy, 0.628 against search-4, 1.000 against random, and 0.215 against stun-first, which now beats greedy 0.886 and search-4 0.950, while pressure-floor beats greedy 0.874 and search-4 falls to 0.485 against it. Search 14 fitted the lookahead's weights on the 20-health content and bought greedy (0.39 to 0.83 on unseen seeds) by giving up stun-first (0.99 to 0.835), which was its check; stun-first is in the panel this time, so the search cannot trade it away. The panel is greedy, stun-first and pressure-floor, the three heuristics that are not beaten by the others at 30 health, a candidate ranking last if it falls below the start against any; random is left out because every set beats it and it costs a third of the budget. The check, off that line, is search-4. The start is the built-in weights and the budget 4 rounds of 10: run 18 asked for 6 rounds of 12, as search 14 had, and the workflow stopped it at three hours after 51 of its 73 candidates, about three and a half minutes each, because a match against stun-first lasts about twice as many rounds as one against greedy. Forty-one candidates leave room for the replay on seeds the search never saw. What would make it a rung: a set that, played as the lookahead, beats stun-first on seeds it never saw without falling below the built-in set against greedy, pressure-floor or the check.
